properties.description:
Implement the system split agreed in chat. The user has delegated the implementation and finer planning; ask only about unresolved user-visible behavior or system boundaries.

SystemEngineering owns Activity board/task graph/repositories, task and review invariants and operations, buildspaces, system dependency graphs, checks and application/component previews. Keep the repository tree here for now. Keep technology-specific parts identifiable without introducing speculative technology contributors.

RelationalUi owns graph editor, feed view/common wrappers, settings and annotations. Producers retain ownership of their feed content, custom presentation and actions. Avoid expanding the deferred feed redesign. Image presentation belongs here; file/image access and filesystem observation belong to FilesystemContributor.

HarnessContributor owns reusable agent execution, model/provider integration and the current chat experience. Only it may depend on Pi; owned public contracts must not expose Pi types or runtime objects. Search the complete repository for other chat/session UI and trace consumers before removing predecessors. Consolidate retained HarnessApp/Harness/Pi functionality. The latest user clarification is to preserve the currently used chat and conversation workflow, including its approval/review behavior; do not retire it merely because its code predates the current Activity board. Remove only confirmed predecessor paths and artifacts.

HarnessContributor and SystemEngineering must work independently: neither depends on the other. A dedicated integration contributor connects their capabilities. Buildspace and engineering functionality must remain usable without AI. New agent scheduling/worktree workflows are outside this task.

Use existing owners for Git/repository composition, persistence, engine lifecycle, HTTP transport/authentication and MCP. Remove HarnessApp's central construction of Planning, Chat and Workflow. Assemble the application through PersoTemplate over BtrTemplate and DefaultTemplate, with a thin executable bootstrap.

Move source and its tests/contracts/configuration to the owning systems; do not leave predecessor wrappers, duplicate implementations or obsolete dependencies. Preserve current user edits and runtime data. Validate retained behavior and dependency direction; build, inspect and run the composed application.

Implementation child tasks are optional and do not require user review. This accepted scope supersedes the earlier assumption that HarnessContributor may depend on SystemEngineering.

Completed implementation (2026-11-07)

HarnessApp and the separate Pi predecessor have been removed from the active composition. SystemEngineering owns engineering workspaces, planning, checks and previews; HarnessContributor owns the retained agent runtime and chat with private Pi integration; EngineeringHarness connects them without either foundational contributor depending on the other. RelationalUi owns the shared presentation, with Filesystem, WebBridge and MCP retaining their respective boundaries. Application startup is composed by PersoTemplate over BtrTemplate and DefaultSuperAppTemplate; the root application.ts is a thin launcher. Current conversations, task/review operations and user data were preserved. The one-off extraction script was removed.

Final code heads: TheBroccoli 4aa928bd; BtrTemplate afe56e0; PersoTemplate c183bdf. Changes were committed in reviewable batches on master. Unrelated live planning-record edits in PersoTemplate were preserved rather than included in source commits.

Verification: final build148 completed successfully; 1,938 authored files passed type safety, dependency-depth organisation passed for 20 systems, and engine-boundary validation reported zero violations. Model generation completed with 953 types from 17 packages. The composed service was restarted and Activity board, repository navigation and the regular source editor were inspected live.

The full application checkpoint initially passed 305 of 307 tests: Windows startup-cancellation timing and a composed-activity Git operation failed in that run; both passed isolated reruns. The full browser run initially passed 416 of 436 tests. All 20 failed browser cases subsequently passed focused reruns after correcting extraction fixtures and repository-view state/lifetime defects. This is not a claim that the full suite was rerun clean after the final corrections. The final repository run passed 16/16 cases, including delayed metadata, retained selection, unsaved-file protection and zero retained retired editor views.

Isolated interaction recording with 400 tasks: selected details 53.8–85.8 ms; confirmed moves 543–744 ms with local pending feedback observed at 110–126 ms. These fixture timings do not claim equivalent cold live-workspace startup performance. The first live source opening after restart still incurred a noticeable cold-load delay.

Evidence: .harness/harness-split/build148.log, checkpoint132.log, composed-activity133.log, startup-cancellation134.log, browser144.log, navigation147.log and the corresponding ApplicationTests/test-results recordings and screenshots.
